subject: 🦃 Tech turkeys

Plus: Black Friday is back | Wednesday, November 25, 2026
 
View in browser
 
 
Axios Closer
By Nathan Bomey · Nov 25, 2026

Wednesday ✅. This year, I am thankful for things like my health and my family — blah, blah, blah. But really, I'm mostly thankful that the Milwaukee Brewers are the World Series champions.

Today's newsletter is 790 words, a 3-minute read.

📉 The dashboard: The S&P 500 closed down 0.3%.

🔥 Today's stock spotlight: SpaceX (+1.3%) received conditional approval by the FCC to deploy 1 million computing satellites into orbit, a key regulatory win for Elon Musk's plan to operate AI data centers in space.
 
 
1 big thing: Tech turkeys
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Stock: Getty Images
 

The economy is hot, but stocks are not.

Why it matters: Concerns about the sustainability of the AI spending binge have been looming over Wall Street for months — and they haven't gone away just because Jensen Huang is back on the job.

🦃 State of play: AI stocks are down in the dumps heading into Thanksgiving, despite signs of a humming economy, as the feverish embrace of Huang's return to Nvidia fades.

  • Those good vibes weren't enough to stave off another tech-led risk-off move in markets.

📉 By the numbers: The Nasdaq 100 index, which represents some of the biggest tech companies, was down as much as 4.7% this morning before closing down 0.6%.

  • It's now down nearly 12% since Huang was ousted (before he wasn't) from Nvidia. (See below.👇)
  • Speaking of Nvidia, today was another particularly ugly one, with the stock closing down 3.9%.
  • The company has now shed nearly $1 trillion in market value since the Huang scandal broke and more than $2 trillion since the stock's October peak.

The latest: The chip giant and center of the AI universe continues to face numerous unanswered questions surrounding the Huang episode.

  • And today, credit ratings firm S&P Global warned it may cut Nvidia's AA rating, citing concerns around its board's independence and "key man" risk related to Huang.

Other AI stocks also swung between big losses and smaller ones today, with the chips sector and hyperscalers particularly volatile.

  • The Magnificent Seven were also feeling the pain, with all but Meta and Apple trading down.

📊 Zoom out: Macro issues also contributed to today's stock volatility.

  • The federal government reported that the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — rose 0.2% from September to 3.8% in October.
  • That likely heightens the chances of a Fed rate hike, putting additional pressure on growth stocks.

Reality check: Outside the tech sector, stocks fared better. Seven of the 11 S&P 500 sectors closed the day in positive territory.

The bottom line: The sugar high that the AI trade got from Huang's stunning reinstatement has given way to a headache.

2. 🎁 Black Friday shows signs of life
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

Maybe Black Friday isn't dead after all.

State of play: The annual post-Thanksgiving shopping extravaganza has declined in significance in recent years as deals have stretched earlier and earlier in the calendar.

  • But this year, 87% of consumers expect to shop from Black Friday through Cyber Monday, "marking the highest levels since 2016," according to Deloitte's survey of 1,200 consumers.
  • One reason: Budget-conscious shoppers are holding out for better deals.

By the numbers: Black Friday slots into an overall holiday shopping season that's expected to top $1 trillion for the first time, according to the National Retail Federation and Bain & Co.

  • Online, consumers spent $82.5 billion in the first 22 days of November, up 9.1% from a year earlier, according to Adobe.

💭 Nathan's thought bubble: I have fond memories of covering the golden days of Black Friday shopping, and I wonder if the nostalgia factor is giving the day a boost again.

3. 🗞️ The readout
 

The 2025 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. Photo: Craig T Fruchtman/Getty Images
 

🦃 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed for the first time in the event's history as a nor'easter bears down on New York. (Axios)

🇯🇵 Starbucks has reportedly tapped advisors to explore a sale of its Japan business. (Bloomberg)

🚙 Amazon Autos is planning to launch its services in the U.K. in early 2027, in what would be its first overseas market expansion. (WSJ)
 
 
4. 🕔 After hours: NBA's Euro step
 

Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios
 

The NBA is aiming to raise at least $10.9 billion to launch a new basketball league in Europe, Bloomberg reported.

State of play: The NBA is hoping to start the European league in October 2027.

  • The league is partnering with financial institutions including Apollo Global Management, Ares Management, Blackstone and JPMorgan Chase.

Reality check: "13 Euroleague shareholder clubs, who already operate a Europe-wide basketball competition, rejected a formal merger with NBA Europe," Bloomberg reported.
